Well, it's early March now, the wheat is just turning green. I've been farming these 10 mu in Quzhou for 40 years, since I was 22. My old man farmed this land before me. I'm 62 this year, middle school education — back then that was enough to get me reading the extension pamphlets, though I don't trust them blindly. I've seen droughts, floods, and years when the bollworm ate everything. I know this soil.

My household is just me and my wife now. Our son works in a factory in Shijiazhuang and sends a little money home, but we can't count on it. I did some construction work in the county town over the winter, earned about 3,500 yuan. That's our input budget for the year, more or less. Every yuan matters. I can't spend it all on fertilizer no matter what the extension guy says — I need to keep some cash for my wife's blood pressure medicine and for emergencies.

**Winter wheat — 8 mu**

The wheat went in last October, same as always. I used Jimai variety, bought seed at about 28 yuan per mu. For base fertilizer I put down 40 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — that's what I've done for years. Now it's green-up time. The wheat looks decent; we had good snow cover this winter, which helps with the moisture.

The extension fellow said I should topdress no more than 25 jin of urea per mu at green-up. But last year I did about 30 jin and got 430 kg per mu, which was better than my neighbor who followed the pamphlet exactly. So I'll put down about 30 jin of urea per mu — that's about 14 kg of nitrogen — when I irrigate at jointing in late March. I'll irrigate three times total: green-up, jointing, and grain filling in May. Water costs keep going up, electricity for the well is 40-50 yuan each time for the whole plot, so three times is my limit. If it rains in April, I might skip the jointing irrigation and save that money for maize. I'll spray herbicide once in early spring, and if I see powdery mildew I'll add fungicide. My wife helps with the spraying. For harvest, I'll hire the combine — costs about 60 yuan per mu but saves my back. I expect around 430 kg per mu if the weather holds.

**Summer maize — 8 mu (same land, after wheat)**

The window between wheat harvest in early June and maize planting is brutal — sometimes five days, that's it. I learned the hard way in 2013 when I was slow and lost yield. I'll use Zhengdan hybrid seed, about 32 yuan per mu. I buy fresh seed every year; saved maize seed is false economy. After the combine goes through the wheat, I'll hire the rotary tiller to chop the straw and loosen the soil — one pass, that's all there's time for. I can't afford no-till equipment, so minimal tillage it is.

Base fertilizer: 35 jin of compound per mu at planting, then topdress with 25 jin of urea at jointing in July. The extension guy says 20 jin urea is enough, but I remember 2016 when I went light and the leaves yellowed. I'd rather waste a little money than lose half the crop. So about 35 jin compound plus 25 jin urea — call it 15 kg nitrogen per mu total. I'll irrigate twice if it doesn't rain: once at jointing, once at filling. Some years one irrigation is enough, but I'm not gambling. One herbicide spray at planting. Harvest is custom combine again. Yield should be around 470 kg per mu, maybe 480 if the summer rains are good.

**Cotton — 2.1 mu (south plot)**

I keep this south plot in cotton even though wheat-maize is easier. Why? Diversification. In 2018 the maize price collapsed and if I hadn't had cotton I'd have lost money that year. Cotton is labor hell, though. My wife handles most of the picking because her hands are quicker than mine. Planting in mid-April, after the wheat topdress is done and I have a breather.

I use improved seed, about 22 yuan per mu. Base of 30 jin compound fertilizer, then two urea topdresses — one at flowering, one at boll stage. Total nitrogen around 28 jin per mu, maybe 13 kg. Cotton needs water at flowering and boll stage, so two irrigations. The bollworm is the enemy — I'll spray insecticide three times, and herbicide twice. The real cost is picking labor. Me and my wife can handle maybe 60% of it, but for the rest I have to hire women from the village at 100 yuan per day. That's my biggest cash outlay for cotton. I expect about 500 jin of seed cotton per mu — 250 kg — which at last year's price should cover the hired labor and leave a little profit.

**The tradeoffs**

Fertilizer prices went up again. If I followed the optimal recommendation I'd spend over 5,000 yuan on inputs alone. I don't have that. I'm targeting about 3,800 yuan total. That means my nitrogen rates are a bit below what the textbook says, but I'm playing it safe where it counts — topdress at jointing, insecticide on cotton. I could push the maize fertilizer higher, but then I'd have to cut cotton pesticide, and one bollworm outbreak would wipe out that 2 mu. I'd rather have slightly lower maize yield and protect the cotton. Water is another constraint — three wheat irrigations plus two each for maize and cotton means the electric bill adds up. I'm watching the sky every day.
